# PROJECT LANTERN 2 STATUS REPORT
## Community Library Appointment Pilot

---

**2026-10-08 | ENTRY 1: PROJECT INITIATION**

Project Lantern 2 kicked off on schedule with full scope definition complete. The pilot aims to test an online appointment booking system for Meridian Valley Public Library's four branch locations. Scope covers: appointment scheduling for reference consultations (30-minute slots), study room reservations (60-minute slots), and computer lab access (45-minute slots). Target user population is 400 patrons across all branches. Backend infrastructure uses existing library database; frontend is web-based React application. Testing will run across three calendar weeks in November, culminating in a two-week internal trial with library staff. Team roster finalized: Marcus Webb (product), Yuki Tanaka (engineering lead), Priya Mendez (QA), David Cho (UX). Initial database schema validated against existing patron records. No blocking issues at launch.

---

**2026-10-15 | ENTRY 2: EARLY TESTING ENVIRONMENT READY**

Staging environment deployed successfully. All four branch locations now have test credentials configured in the database. Priya's QA team ran initial smoke tests: appointment creation, calendar rendering, time-slot conflict detection, and user authentication. Results: 47 test cases executed, 43 passed. Four failures identified were environment setup issues, not application bugs. Database performance baseline established: average query response time 140ms for availability checks, 95ms for slot booking. Redis caching layer tested with 500 concurrent user simulation; cache hit ratio 87% under normal load. Team identified need for additional testing on mobile browsers (iOS Safari, Android Chrome). Scheduled secondary round of compatibility testing for week of 2026-10-22. Preliminary documentation drafted for internal testers.

---

**2026-10-22 | ENTRY 3: USER ACCEPTANCE TESTING PHASE ONE COMPLETE**

First round of UAT concluded with 12 volunteer library staff members using the system for five days. Participants conducted 156 total booking transactions: 89 reference consultations, 51 study room reservations, 16 computer lab bookings. System stability solid; no crashes recorded. Users reported interface clarity as "good" or "excellent" in 94% of feedback surveys. Booking workflow intuitive for most; 11 of 12 participants completed first appointment without guidance. Mobile experience validated across iOS 17 and Android 14. Average booking time: 2 minutes 45 seconds from login to confirmation. One recurring user comment: unclear what happens after canceling an appointment. Three staff members reported confusion about whether cancellation email would auto-send. This prompted closer investigation into our cancellation flow logic.

---

**2026-10-28 | ENTRY 4: CANCELLATION FLOW GAP IDENTIFIED**

During post-UAT review, Yuki discovered a critical gap in the cancellation pathway. System allows users to cancel appointments with one-click confirmation, but the notification dispatch sequence has a hidden dependency: cancellation email triggers only after database record deletion completes, which happens asynchronously in a background job queue. In current testing, 87% of cancellations processed email within 60 seconds, but 13% show delays of 4-8 minutes. Worse: if patron closes browser immediately after clicking "confirm cancellation," they receive no visual confirmation that the action registered. No data loss occurs; the appointment is removed from the database correctly. However, user experience is ambiguous. Priya's logs revealed two UAT instances where patrons attempted to re-book the same slot, suggesting they doubted the cancellation succeeded. This gap was not caught in earlier testing because team did not explicitly test the cancellation scenario or measure email send latency under realistic timing conditions.

---

**2026-10-31 | ENTRY 5: ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS AND REPAIR PLAN**

Root cause confirmed: the background job queue uses a standard FIFO processor with no prioritization tier. Cancellation notifications are treated identically to other transactional emails (appointment confirmations, reminder notifications). During peak testing hours (11:00-14:00), queue depth reached 320+ items, causing 10-minute total latencies. Secondary issue: user-facing confirmation message appears immediately after button click, but that message does not indicate whether email dispatch succeeded or is pending. Solution design approved: (1) separate cancellation emails into a priority queue; (2) add post-cancellation modal showing explicit confirmation status ("Email sent," "Sending...," or "Retry" if failure detected); (3) add retry logic for failed email sends within 5 minutes. Estimated implementation effort: 12 hours of engineering work plus 6 hours of QA validation. No database schema changes required. Yuki committed to delivery by 2026-11-05.

---

**2026-11-01 | ENTRY 6: CANCELLATION REPAIR IMPLEMENTATION BEGUN**

Yuki and junior engineer Raj Patel began implementing the three-part repair. Priority queue infrastructure deployed in staging; refactored email dispatcher to route cancellations to priority channel. Confirmation modal UI designed by David, approved by Marcus without design iteration. Modal includes three states: success (green checkmark, "Cancellation confirmed"), pending (spinner, "Sending confirmation..."), and retry prompt (orange warning, retry button). Implementation revealed one unexpected coupling: the existing appointment confirmation modal uses different visual language. Decided to update both modals to consistent design system rather than maintain two patterns. This added 2 hours to scope but reduces future maintenance debt. Retry logic completed; tested with simulated queue failures. Database indexes verified; no performance regression detected in staging. Code review scheduled for 2026-11-03. Current status: 68% complete.

---

**2026-11-03 | ENTRY 7: REPAIR VALIDATION AND EDGE CASE TESTING**

Repair code merged after peer review. Yuki and Priya executed expanded cancellation test suite: 247 cancellation transactions under varying conditions. Test matrix included: normal operation, queue under load (simulated 500-item backlog), email service degradation (50% delivery failure), network latency injection (250ms+ delays), and rapid re-booking attempts (user canceling and rebooking same slot within 30 seconds). Results: 243 of 247 tests passed. Four failures were retry-logic edge cases where a cancellation email failed, user clicked retry, but original record was already reprocessed. Fixed with idempotency key in email dispatch. Modal confirmation displayed correctly in 100% of test runs; state transitions smooth. Email latency under test load: 89% of cancellations now receive email within 12 seconds; 99th percentile latency is 35 seconds. Mobile modal rendering tested on iOS 17 and Android 14; no layout breakage. One unresolved issue: if user has notification delivery disabled in browser settings, no email is sent but modal still shows "Sending..." indefinitely (waiting for email system ACK). Noted as known limitation for post-launch iteration.

---

**2026-11-04 | ENTRY 8: EVIDENCE REVIEW AND TESTING LIMITATIONS**

QA team reviewed complete test evidence and identified scope limitations in our validation approach. Testing was conducted in staging with synthetic data (no real patron history, no production database load patterns). Simulated load testing used uniform random booking distribution; real library usage likely has temporal clustering (morning rush, lunch hour, evening). Email service testing used mock SMTP server; production uses Mailgun API with real network variability we cannot fully replicate. Only 4 of 12 original UAT participants available for repair validation; we did not retest with full original cohort. Mobile testing limited to two platforms; older Android versions (9-10) untested due to CI environment constraints. Retry logic was tested with injected failures but not against real email service degradation (e.g., Mailgun rate limits). These limitations are documented but do not invalidate the repair; they indicate that full confidence in cancellation reliability under real production conditions will only come after live monitoring post-launch. Proposed mitigation: add monitoring dashboard for email dispatch latency and failure rates, with alerting if 99th percentile exceeds 60 seconds.

---

**2026-11-05 | ENTRY 9: READINESS ASSESSMENT AND CAPTAIN DECISION PENDING**

Repair validation complete. System is ready for internal trial as scheduled. Cancellation flow now meets design criteria: user receives prompt visual confirmation, email delivery is prioritized and retried, and edge cases are documented. Marcus convened readiness review: no blocking issues remain. Proposed timeline: launch internal trial with library staff on 2026-11-12 for two weeks (through 2026-11-25). Trial will involve 25 staff testers rotating through all four branches, booking real appointments and canceling 20% of them to exercise repaired flow. Trial success criteria: (1) zero reported cancellation confirmation failures, (2) email delivery latency under 60 seconds for 99% of cancellations, (3) no crashes or data inconsistencies, (4) user satisfaction score 4.0+ out of 5. Marcus has flagged the trial schedule to the library director and is awaiting final approval. This decision rests with the library Captain (Director Eva Santos). Pending her confirmation by end of business 2026-11-05.

---

**2026-11-05 | ENTRY 10: TRIAL POSTPONEMENT IMPACT ANALYSIS**

If Director Santos postpones the internal trial beyond 2026-11-12, consequences cascade. Current team availability is constrained after 2026-11-25; Yuki transitions to a separate project (Building Initiative Q5 planning), and Priya has vacation scheduled 2026-11-26 through 2026-12-09. Restarting trial in December would require rebuilding test cohort and re-training new participants. Library branch closures 2026-12-20 through 2026-01-02 eliminate testing opportunity during peak winter patron activity. Postponement also delays go-live beyond target of 2026-12-15, pushing public availability into January when library seasonal usage dips, reducing real-world validation window. Public launch currently scheduled for 2026-12-22 assuming trial completes on time and no critical issues emerge. A two-week postponement compresses validation timeline and increases risk of launching with undetected production issues. Technical repairs are complete and stable; delay does not improve system quality. Team recommendation: proceed with trial on 2026-11-12 as planned. Awaiting Captain decision.

---

**END OF REPORT**

PROJECT LANTERN 3 - STATUS REPORT
Community Library Appointment Pilot
Reporting Period: 2026-10-01 through 2026-11-05

---

ENTRY 1 - 2026-10-01 - PROJECT KICKOFF AND SCOPE DEFINITION

Project Lantern 3 launched today with formal scope approval. The pilot targets three branch locations in the Riverside County library system: Central Downtown, Mill Creek Community, and Westridge Educational Hub. The system allows patrons to book reference librarian consultations, study room reservations, and technology training sessions through a web interface and SMS fallback. Scope includes appointment scheduling, patron notification via email and text, staff confirmation workflows, and basic reporting dashboards. The pilot runs for twelve weeks with target enrollment of 120 active patrons across all three branches. Success criteria are defined as ninety percent patron satisfaction on post-visit surveys, eighty-five percent on-time arrival rates, and zero critical system failures during operating hours. Staff capacity is three full-time developers, one QA engineer, two library liaison managers, and rotating librarian stakeholder participation. Budget allocation covers development infrastructure, SMS gateway costs, and staff time through December 2026. Expected completion is feature-complete by 2026-11-15 with live traffic acceptance running through 2026-12-20.

---

ENTRY 2 - 2026-10-08 - INITIAL SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE AND COMPONENT TESTING

Development completed the core system architecture this week. The appointment booking engine accepts reservations through three channels: web portal, phone hotline with voice menu, and email request with automated parsing. The backend uses PostgreSQL for appointment storage with redundant backups. Frontend styling follows county accessibility standards, WCAG 2.1 AA compliance validated at component level. Automated test suite for booking logic reached eighty-two percent code coverage with unit tests for time conflict detection, timezone handling, and patron eligibility validation. Manual testing began on the web interface with three test scenarios per librarian role: reference consultant, facilities coordinator, and branch supervisor. Initial accessibility audit showed five minor color contrast issues and two missing alt text labels, all tagged for remediation. SMS notification service integrated with Twilio using production credentials in sandbox mode. First mock appointment cycle completed successfully with fifty test bookings, automated confirmations, and reminders working as designed. Staff conducted initial usability interviews with eight library employees, collecting feedback on dashboard navigation and reporting features.

---

ENTRY 3 - 2026-10-15 - EXTENDED INTEGRATION TESTING AND PATRON WORKFLOW DISCOVERY

Extended integration testing revealed the interconnection between appointment confirmation and the patron information database. A complete end-to-end workflow was tested: patron books appointment via web portal, system validates availability, patron receives email confirmation with calendar invite, librarian receives staff notification, appointment appears on branch calendar, and reminder SMS sends twenty-four hours before scheduled time. Testing uncovered a minor race condition when two patrons booked the same time slot simultaneously, now fixed by adding database-level locking. The team conducted two rounds of user acceptance testing with twelve volunteer patrons from the local community, each completing four test bookings across different appointment types. Patrons reported average task completion time of four minutes for web booking and seven minutes for phone booking due to menu navigation. The reporting dashboard was tested with six months of simulated historical data, showing capacity utilization charts, no-show analysis, and patron retention trends. One integration point required rework: the study room availability feed was initially pulling stale data from a nightly batch job, now replaced with real-time queries. Staff conducted competency training with all three branch locations, covering appointment approval workflows, patron communication, and emergency cancellation procedures.

---

ENTRY 4 - 2026-10-22 - DISCOVERY OF CANCELLATION FLOW GAP AND IMPACT ASSESSMENT

A critical workflow gap was discovered during stress testing this week. The cancellation flow had no defined handling for cases where a patron cancels within two hours of their appointment time. Current system sends a notification to the librarian but does not automatically open the time slot for rebooking; the slot remains marked as reserved but empty. Manual reclassification requires librarian intervention in the admin panel, which takes approximately eight minutes per incident. Testing simulated one hundred cancellations with varying time windows. Results showed that forty-two percent of cancellations occurred within four hours of appointment time, with fifteen percent occurring less than two hours before. If librarians miss reclassifying a slot, the appointment calendar shows false occupancy for that day, blocking new patron bookings. This directly conflicts with the scope requirement for appointment availability accuracy. Additionally, duplicate cancellation requests can occur when patrons use both the web portal and phone hotline, causing data inconsistency. The QA team documented three scenarios where this occurred during testing, each requiring manual database correction. The gap creates downstream reporting errors: no-show counts include unavailable librarians, utilization rates appear artificially low, and capacity planning dashboards show inaccurate demand patterns.

---

ENTRY 5 - 2026-10-29 - CANCELLATION FLOW REPAIR IMPLEMENTATION AND VERIFICATION

The cancellation flow repair was implemented and tested this week. The solution includes three components: an automated time-slot re-opening mechanism that triggers immediately upon patron cancellation regardless of timing, a duplicate-request guard using idempotent operation keys in the database, and a librarian notification system that batches slot openings into a single daily summary email rather than individual interruptions. The automated mechanism was built using a SQL trigger that executes transactionally when a cancellation record is inserted, ensuring atomic updates. The duplicate guard checks for existing cancellation requests from the same patron for the same appointment within a one-minute window, preventing accidental re-submissions. Testing of the repair included regression suite execution with fifteen hundred appointment lifecycle scenarios, covering all combinations of booking, confirmation, reminder, and cancellation. The automated reclassification was validated against manual reclassification in five hundred test cases, confirming identical results. Performance testing showed the new trigger adds less than one millisecond to the cancellation operation. The team tested edge cases including same-day rebooking by the original patron, cascading cancellations when a librarian cancels, and concurrent cancellation requests from the system and patron. All cases now process without manual intervention. QA conducted two verification cycles with the librarian staff using live data from the volunteer patron testing, confirming that no manual reclassification occurred in seventy-eight test cancellations across the four-hour and two-hour windows.

---

ENTRY 6 - 2026-11-01 - EVIDENCE LIMITATIONS AND DATA QUALITY CONSTRAINTS

Documentation of evidence limitations and data quality constraints was completed this week to ensure realistic scope of validation claims. The volunteer patron pool includes only forty-two individuals who responded to community outreach, predominantly in the age range thirty-five to sixty-five; younger patrons and non-English speakers are underrepresented. Simulated historical data used in testing was generated synthetically based on assumptions about typical library traffic patterns and seasonal variation; no actual patron behavior data from equivalent systems was available for calibration. Testing conducted in controlled environments with dedicated test accounts does not replicate real network conditions, concurrent user loads beyond fifty simultaneous users, or mobile network quality variance. SMS delivery reliability was tested only with Twilio sandbox endpoints; production SMS behavior depends on carrier routing decisions outside system scope. The automated cancellation trigger was tested with PostgreSQL version thirteen; library systems use version twelve in production, and backward compatibility cannot be fully verified without production deployment. Staff competency training covered only three specific branches; two additional branches may join the pilot after week six if enrollment targets are met, and their staff training needs may differ. The accessibility audit was conducted remotely using automated scanning and manual spot-checks; in-person testing with users who have visual or motor disabilities has not occurred. Calendar invite integration depends on email client software at patron's home; delivery success rates depend on spam filter tuning, proxy server configuration, and other elements outside project scope.

---

ENTRY 7 - 2026-11-02 - PREPARATION FOR INTERNAL TRIAL AND SCOPE CONFIRMATION

The project is ready for internal trial commencement with formal scope confirmation completed. Internal trial will run for two weeks using real patron traffic at Central Downtown branch location only, with volunteer staff participation. The trial will operate during extended hours Monday through Saturday, ten a.m. through six p.m., with librarian coverage by four scheduled staff members. Trial success criteria include: zero critical system failures, response time under three seconds for ninety-fifth percentile requests, automated cancellation reclassification occurring in one hundred percent of late cancellations without manual intervention, patron satisfaction survey average of four point two or higher on five-point scale, and staff satisfaction survey confirming workflow integration feasibility. Data collection during trial includes response time telemetry, error logs, patron satisfaction surveys administered on-site with QR code linking to online form, staff feedback sessions scheduled for days four, nine, and fourteen, and hourly system utilization reporting. The trial is resource-intensive: full QA presence on-site for first three days, on-call support for remaining eleven days, daily report generation and analysis, and staff coordination meetings every other day. Trial commencement requires Captain approval and final sign-off on resource allocation. If trial is postponed by one week, the project completion deadline compresses to four weeks, eliminating the planned two-week contingency period and eliminating the secondary branch testing phase originally scheduled for weeks nine through eleven.

---

ENTRY 8 - 2026-11-03 - PENDING CAPTAIN DECISION BRIEFING

Captain decision required this week on internal trial commencement timing and scope. Two decisions are coupled: approval to start the internal trial on 2026-11-06 depends on confirming resource availability from existing development staff, and this allocation directly impacts secondary branch on-site training completion by 2026-11-12. The trial will consume thirty percent of QA capacity, twenty percent of developer time for on-call support, and one hundred percent of one liaison manager for coordination. Development schedule shows three feature items remain as stretch goals: advanced reporting with custom date ranges, bulk appointment import for partner organizations, and patron preference persistence across sessions. These will be deferred if trial proceeds as scheduled; if trial is postponed, these items can complete in parallel during trial preparation extension. The decision framework: confirm trial start date by 2026-11-05 end of business, or communicate delay to volunteer partners with revised timeline. If trial is postponed by one week, the project absorbs the delay into week nine, compressing the post-trial adjustment period from ten days to three days and eliminating planned staff retraining on system improvements identified during trial.

---

ENTRY 9 - 2026-11-04 - TRIAL READINESS VERIFICATION AND DOCUMENTATION

Trial readiness verification completed today with all checklist items passing. Production environment configured with dedicated database instance, SSL certificates valid through 2027, backup schedule set for daily execution, and disaster recovery procedures documented with recovery time objective of two hours. Monitoring dashboard set up tracking system response times, error rates, database connection counts, SMS delivery status, and email transmission logs. On-call support contacts established with escalation path: QA engineer first, tech lead second, project manager third. Client communication template prepared for daily trial reports sent to library administration, covering usage statistics, any issues encountered, and emerging requirements. Volunteer staff completed three-hour orientation covering system navigation, staff workflows, patron communication, and emergency procedures. Orientation completion rate: one hundred percent of scheduled staff, with proficiency test average score of eighty-six percent. All staff demonstrated competency with appointment approval workflow. Documentation finalized: technical architecture guide, staff user manual with screenshots, troubleshooting guide for common issues, patron quick-start guide, and administrative procedures for settings changes. Communication sent to enrolled patrons explaining trial expectations, system features, and feedback survey process. Volunteer patron response rate to survey pre-trial questions: sixty-seven percent completion rate. Technical validation complete: system load testing showed capacity for one hundred fifty concurrent users without performance degradation, database query optimization reduced average response time to one point eight seconds, and error recovery procedures tested across five failure scenarios with all tests passing.

---

ENTRY 10 - 2026-11-05 - FINAL STATUS AND CAPTAIN DECISION SUMMARY

Project status as of today: feature development complete, testing complete, internal trial preparation complete, all scope gates passed. System is ready for Captain approval to commence two-week internal trial beginning 2026-11-06 at Central Downtown branch. The cancellation flow repair is verified and operational. Evidence limitations are documented: volunteer population is small and unrepresentative, historical data is synthetic, production-scale behavior remains untested, and accessibility with diverse user populations is incomplete. Trial will generate data to address population representativeness and production-scale performance. If trial proceeds on schedule, project timeline remains intact with post-trial adjustment period running 2026-11-20 through 2026-11-25, secondary branch ramp-up starting 2026-11-26, and live traffic acceptance by 2026-12-20. If trial is postponed by one week, secondary branch ramp-up compresses into three days or eliminates entirely, eliminating validation at additional locations and increasing risk of branch-specific issues being discovered after go-live rather than during controlled testing. Captain decision required by end of business today: approve trial start 2026-11-06, or communicate revised timeline. Remaining decision: defer stretch goal features (advanced reporting, bulk import, preference persistence) during active trial, or add two developers to parallel development track.

---

END OF REPORT

Sprint 2 progress mixed. Notification subsystem fully deployed and tested end-to-end with municipal SMS provider (Clarity Messaging). Confirmation flow completed: patrons receive email confirmation immediately upon booking, SMS reminder 24 hours before appointment, and post-appointment satisfaction survey link. Confirmation email open rate measured at 64% in staging environment (measured across 287 test messages, October 2-5). SMS delivery rate at 98.3% (one message failed due to invalid phone format in test data). Appointment confirmation feature stories delivered on time. Cancellation workflow, however, encountered scope creep: product team identified seven distinct cancellation scenarios (patron self-service, staff-initiated for emergencies, automatic timeout for no-shows, administrative bulk cancellations, system-generated due to staff unavailability, rescheduling-as-cancellation, and patron request via phone bridge). Initial estimates covered only patron self-service and staff emergency cancellation. Remaining five scenarios require additional database migration and state machine complexity. Cancellation work deferred to sprint 3; this delays critical path by one sprint. Engineering velocity: 11 of 13 points. Database now contains 52 tables. Automated test suite expanded to 184 test cases; code coverage 76%. Mobile testing expanded to include accessibility checks (WCAG 2.1 AA compliance in progress, 82% of checks passing). Staff calendar sync retry logic performing well; zero timeout failures observed across 4,201 synchronization cycles in staging.

---

## ENTRY 4: 2026-10-20

CRITICAL ISSUE IDENTIFIED: During sprint 3 cancellation workflow development, QA uncovered a gap in the no-show timeout path. The scenario: appointment scheduled, patron fails to arrive at scheduled time, system should auto-cancel after 30-minute grace period and free the slot for other patrons. The gap occurs when system attempts to cancel: current state machine does not emit cancellation notifications to freed slots in adjacent appointment windows. Concretely, if a 60-minute appointment at 2:00 PM times out, the system marks the appointment cancelled but does not re-advertise the 2:00-2:30 and 2:30-3:00 windows back to the available-slots queue. This causes those windows to remain unavailable in the patron-facing UI despite staff member being idle. Gap discovered during scenario testing on October 18 during manual test run by QA lead Maria Chen. Reproduction steps: (1) book appointment for service, (2) reach appointment time in staging environment (time-travel via test harness), (3) wait 31 minutes, (4) query available slots for same service/staff/day, (5) slots do not appear. Tested across all three branches; gap reproduced 100% of test attempts (8 attempts total). Root cause: cancellation event handler at queue-management layer missing integration point. Fix implemented October 19: added eventEmitter.emit('slots_freed') call in cancellation handler, routing freed windows back through availability-compute microservice. No database migration required. Post-fix validation: 12 manual test runs all correct; slots reappear in patron UI within 3 seconds of timeout trigger. Automated regression test added to prevent recurrence. This gap would have caused significant pilot friction: orphaned staff time would compound daily, creating perception of unavailable capacity. Repair completed; release candidate now includes fix.

---

## ENTRY 5: 2026-11-01

Sprint 3 completed with cancellation workflow fully operational. All seven cancellation scenarios implemented and tested. Patron self-service cancellation allows booking revision up to 24 hours before appointment; cancellations within 24 hours flagged as late-notice and captured for operational review. Staff emergency cancellation (immediate) tested under simulated outage conditions: 15-minute cascade email sent to all affected patrons, automatic SMS to high-priority bookings (same-day or critical services). Rescheduling-as-cancellation path integrated; patron rebooking flow completed in single UI transaction. Administrative bulk cancellation (used for branch closures or staff leave) tested with 150-slot cancellations; processing time 2.1 seconds. Phone-bridge cancellation (staff fielding patron requests over phone) partially automated with manual confirmation step. Automatic timeout-based cancellations running in staging; tested across 430 timeout events, all handled correctly with zero missed notifications. Code coverage: 81%. Database schema now 54 tables. Total automated tests: 218. Performance baseline: availability query 285ms average (improved from 340ms in September), cancellation processing 1.2 seconds per event. Manual regression testing across all three branches (Central, Riverside, Hillcrest) conducted October 27-November 1 by combined QA and product team (35 test cases per branch). One minor UI bug found in cancellation confirmation modal (text truncation on longer service names); fixed and revalidated. System declared ready for internal pilot on November 1.

---

## ENTRY 6: 2026-11-03

Internal pilot launch approved by Captain Victoria Ramos on November 2. Pilot scope: live scheduling at Central Library for reference consultation and computer literacy training only (limiting initial demand footprint). Staff volunteers: 8 librarians across three shifts. Real patron bookings enabled November 3 starting 9:00 AM. First-day metrics: 47 appointments booked across two service types, 3 cancellations (all patron-initiated self-service, each within 24-hour window). Cancellation notifications delivered within 4 minutes of action; one SMS delivery delayed to 47 minutes (investigated, Clarity Messaging attributed to queue backlog, not our code). No system errors logged. Appointment confirmation emails sent and opened: 44 of 47 (93.6% open rate within 2 hours, higher than staging 64% - likely reflects real patron engagement). Staff reports good experience with availability display; librarians confirmed they could see opening windows clearly and no schedule conflicts occurred despite manual calendar integration. One staff member reported confusion about rescheduling workflow (product team to review UX), resolved with brief phone training. Notification delays being monitored closely; current 24-hour average: 98.1% SMS delivery within 5 minutes, 100% email delivery within 2 minutes. Database performing well under live load: query response times 312ms average (within bounds). Zero unplanned outages. Monitoring dashboards reporting nominal operation. Pilot satisfaction survey sent to early adopters; 6 responses received (small sample), all positive. Next milestone: extend pilot to document scanning service (45 min appointments) on November 5 pending Captain approval.

---

## ENTRY 7: 2026-11-04

System under live operation for 24 hours. Pilot expanded slightly today: document scanning service (45-minute appointments) added at 10:00 AM. Two additional staff members (scanning specialists) volunteered. Second-day metrics: 23 new appointments booked (total 70 active bookings), 2 cancellations (1 patron self-service, 1 staff-initiated emergency due to equipment failure). Emergency cancellation tested under unplanned stress: staff member cancelled a 2:00 PM scanning slot due to scanner malfunction. Cascade email triggered to three affected patrons within 61 seconds; all three were offered alternative time windows automatically. Two rebooked immediately via UI, one requested phone assistance (handled by reference desk staff). No technical failures during this event. Performance holding steady: 298ms average query time, database CPU utilization 34%. Automated alerts triggered twice during day: one false positive (database connection pool spike that self-resolved), one real alert (notification queue backing up briefly during high-volume confirmation period - 10:30-11:00 AM). Queue recovery to normal depth: 7 minutes. Root cause of queue spike: Clarity Messaging experienced transient slowdown (confirmed via their status page). Our retry logic absorbed the delay without data loss. Code review completed for database migration scripts targeting November 8 deployment window (new pilot metrics table for capture additional operational data). Migration scripts validated in staging environment replica. Vendor credential renewal for SMS service (Clarity) confirmed through November 2027; no interruption risk. Staff volunteers continuing to report positive experience.

---

## ENTRY 8: 2026-11-04 (EVENING)

Evidence limitation discovered during evening operations review. Pilot metrics collected since November 3 are statistically thin: 70 total appointments across 24 hours, drawn from only 10 patron-volunteers and 8 staff members. Cancellation data reflects exactly 2 patron-initiated and 2 staff-initiated events - insufficient for pattern analysis. Specifically, the cancellation-flow repair tested extensively in September-October relied on timeout scenarios (grace-period expiration), but the live pilot has yet to produce a real timeout-based cancellation under normal conditions. The October fix for the state-machine gap was validated against 12 manual test timeouts and 430 staging timeouts, but the specific sequence of events (timeout trigger, slot re-advertisement, patron re-booking the freed slot) has not been observed in production with real patron behavior. Automated monitoring shows the timeout handler firing (zero missed timeouts detected), but actual patron uptake of re-advertised slots has not yet been measured. Current operational window too narrow: we have bookings, cancellations, and notifications confirmed to work, but the end-to-end cancellation-recovery cycle (timeout -> free slots -> patron rebooking) remains untested under real-world conditions. Additional data collection will be required to fully validate the October repair. Estimated time to accumulate sufficient timeout-driven cancellation events: 7-10 days at current booking volume (requires approximately 8-12 no-show events). This limitation is documented in the November 8 Captain decision brief.

---

## ENTRY 9: 2026-11-05

Project Lantern 4 internal pilot now in day 3 of operation. Cumulative bookings: 117 appointments. Staff coverage expanded to include Riverside Branch starting this morning (adding 4 additional staff volunteers, 2 service types). Central Library and Riverside Branch both reporting smooth operations with no critical incidents. Third major cancellation scenario observed today: system-generated automatic cancellation due to staff unavailability (staff member called in sick at 7:30 AM, appointment window for 10:00 AM reference consultation affected). System detected unavailability through staff calendar integration, triggered automatic cancellation of single affected slot, cascade email delivered to patron within 73 seconds, patron rebooked immediately for afternoon window. This scenario validates a key workflow that had been tested extensively but never observed in live operation. Performance metrics holding strong: 94% of appointment confirmations opened within 2 hours, 99.2% SMS delivery within 5 minutes, 100% email delivery, zero unplanned outages. Database health nominal. Monitoring alerts trending down (yesterdays' false positives eliminated via tuning). One minor UX issue captured by staff: rescheduling confirmation modal closes too quickly on some devices, occasionally confusing staff about whether action completed; product team investigating (likely CSS animation timing, non-critical). Pilot satisfaction survey now showing 23 responses across staff and early-adopter patrons; average satisfaction 4.2/5.0, primary praise for ease of use and reliable notifications. Captain Ramos has scheduled November 8 decision briefing to determine trial expansion: proceed to full Hillcrest Commons launch (currently excluded, would add 100+ potential daily bookings) versus continue single-location controlled pilot through November 30.

---

## ENTRY 10: 2026-11-05 (DECISION BRIEFING SUMMARY)

Briefing prepared for Captain Ramos (scheduled November 8, 2:00 PM). Decision point: approve expansion of internal trial to full three-branch deployment with all five service types (reference consultation, computer literacy training, document scanning, children's story hour, and intake appointments), targeting November 8 launch, OR defer expansion to November 15 pending accumulation of additional production data under current controlled scope.

EXPANSION APPROVAL CASE: Three days of successful operation, 117 appointments processed error-free, all critical workflows validated (scheduling, notifications, patron/staff cancellation, emergency scenarios, automatic timeouts). Performance metrics and infrastructure handling current load without stress. Staff training burden minimal (7-minute onboarding sufficient). Technical readiness high. Pilot feedback positive. Estimated immediate benefit: 200+ daily bookings across full district, demonstrating district-wide viability within timeline for spring rollout decision.

DEFERRAL CASE: Cancellation-flow repair (October gap fix) not yet validated under full no-show timeout scenarios with real patron re-booking behavior. Current dataset insufficient: only 2 spontaneous no-show timeout cancellations observed, both too recent for patron reuse pattern analysis. Expansion would increase confidence risk (more staff, more bookings, more edge cases). Seven-day deferral allows accumulation of 8-12 timeout-driven cancellation events, sufficient for pattern validation. Minimal operational cost: pilot remains functional, staff volunteers willing to continue, patrons retain quality service. Risk of deferral: delays final rollout decision by one week, compresses November contingency buffer for any discovered issues.

RECOMMENDATION: Defer expansion to November 15 pending evidence accumulation. Core workflows validated; timeout-recovery evidence gap is narrow and resolvable within deferral window. Single gap represents material risk if expanded prematurely to high-volume deployment. If trial deferred, real-world timeout cancellation patterns will be observable by November 11, triggering full expansion confidence by November 15. If trial proceeds with expansion November 8 as scheduled, system will operate under conditions where the timeout-recovery repair has not been observed in production, carrying unknown operational risk and potential November rollout delay if issues emerge. Recommendation documents evidence limiter and proposes data-driven decision gate for November 8 morning (proceeding based on overnight timeout statistics).

---

End Report

PROJECT LANTERN 5 STATUS REPORT
Community Library Appointment Pilot
Reporting Period: October 8 - November 5, 2026

================================================================================

ENTRY 1: October 8, 2026

Project Lantern 5 entered active development phase this week following approval of
scope from the steering committee. The pilot targets three fictional library branches
in the Portland metro area: Eastlake, Riverdale, and Whitmore. Scope covers: (1)
appointment booking for study room reservations, (2) staff shift management and
availability rules, (3) patron cancellation and rescheduling, (4) email notification
delivery, and (5) basic conflict detection to prevent double-booking. Target launch
is January 15, 2027. Development team is four engineers and one product lead. Backend
uses Node.js with PostgreSQL; frontend is React. Baseline database schema completed
and migrated to staging. Five core tables created: Locations, StaffShifts, Patrons,
Appointments, and NotificationLogs. Schema review was conducted by lead architect
Miranda Vasquez with no blocking concerns raised. Three non-blocking schema notes were
logged about indexing strategy on the Appointments table for query performance at scale.
Code review process will use the standard three-reviewer gate. Initial sprint planning
meeting scheduled for October 15. Current blockers: none. Team morale is positive; two
team members (Kai and Sophia) expressed confidence in the technology choices at standup.

================================================================================

ENTRY 2: October 15, 2026

Sprint 1 began with focus on core appointment create and read flows. Engineering
completed design document for the appointment creation API endpoint. Endpoint will
accept patron ID, location ID, requested time slot, and duration preference. Validation
rules drafted: patrons must have active library card status; requested time must fall
within staff shift hours; no overlapping bookings by same patron within 30 minutes. API
contract was reviewed by backend lead James Chen and approved with minor documentation
clarifications. Frontend kickoff meeting held to scope the booking interface. Product
lead Amelia Rodriguez defined the happy path: patron logs in, selects location from
dropdown menu, views available time slots for next 14 days, clicks to book, receives
confirmation. Three frontend engineers began implementing React component scaffolding.
Database seeding script created to populate test data: 15 fictional patron accounts
(test-patron-001 through test-patron-015), 12 staff shift records per location, and
pre-generated 1000 candidate appointment slots. Test database deployed to staging
environment. Initial build runs passed without errors. One toolchain issue noted: Jest
snapshot testing required explicit regeneration on M2 Mac machines due to file path
normalization differences. Workaround documented in team wiki. Sprint capacity: 32
story points allocated. Burn-down tracking begins next week.

================================================================================

ENTRY 3: October 22, 2026

Sprint 1 completed with 28 story points delivered. Appointment creation endpoint fully
functional and deployed to staging. API integration tests written for: valid booking
(pass), patron without active card (correctly rejects), overlapping time slot (correctly
rejects), and boundary case of exactly 30-minute gap (correctly accepts). Frontend
booking form component working end-to-end in development environment. Amelia conducted
user acceptance testing with three fictional patron personas (busy professional, casual
reader, student researcher). All three completed bookings successfully on first attempt.
No usability blockers identified. Sprint retrospective noted that initial database
queries were running slowly (~800ms for availability slot queries across 1000 slot
records); James optimized the query with composite index on (location_id, start_time,
is_available) and achieved 45ms query time, well within acceptable range. Bug logged
during testing: email notification for confirmation was not sending; root cause was
hardcoded SMTP server address pointing to non-existent internal mail relay. Configuration
externalized to environment variables and SMTP connectivity verified against staging
mail server. No data quality issues in staging database. Sprint 2 planning scheduled for
October 29. Forecast for next sprint: cancellation flows, rescheduling, and integration
testing between booking and notification systems.

================================================================================

ENTRY 4: October 29, 2026

Sprint 2 began with intentional focus on patron cancellation workflows. This is a
critical feature for library operations because patrons frequently need to cancel
bookings due to schedule conflicts. Product requirements state: patron can cancel up to
30 minutes before appointment start time; system sends cancellation confirmation email;
time slot becomes available for other patrons; all cancellation events logged for audit.
Cancellation endpoint designed and coded. Kai led implementation of the rescheduling
logic: patron selects existing appointment, clicks Reschedule, system presents available
alternative slots within 7 days of original booking, patron selects new time, original
appointment released, new appointment created, confirmation email sent. Backend code
review by James identified one edge case: if a patron attempted to reschedule to the
exact same time slot while another patron was clicking to book it, a race condition
could create two overlapping appointments. Resolved with database-level unique constraint
on (location_id, start_time) and optimistic locking pattern on the appointment record.
Sophia wrote integration tests covering: successful cancellation, failed cancellation
(too close to start time), successful reschedule, reschedule to unavailable slot (reject),
and simultaneous book/reschedule race condition (verified constraint prevents double-book).
All tests passing. Staging deployment successful. No data corruption observed in 200-slot
load test. One minor issue: cancellation email template had incorrect patron name variable
binding; fixed immediately by Amelia. Forecast looks strong for February trial prep.

================================================================================

ENTRY 5: November 1, 2026

Routine regression testing and exploratory testing uncovered a critical gap in the
cancellation flow. During end-to-end testing of a complete patron lifecycle (book,
confirm, reschedule, cancel), QA engineer Marcus discovered that while the backend
correctly released the appointment slot when a patron cancelled, the notification system
was not alerting other patrons who had previously viewed that time slot as unavailable.
Specifically: Patron A books 2pm slot. System marks 2pm as booked. Patron B views
availability, sees 2pm unavailable, selects 2:30pm instead. Patron A cancels their 2pm
appointment. Patron B has no way to know 2pm is now available and remains booked into
2:30pm suboptimally. No data was lost, but the user experience degraded significantly
because the pilot was designed to maximize utilization across available hours. Additional
investigation revealed the cancellation flow had no mechanism for notifying nearby patrons
or triggering a general "slot availability updated" broadcast. Root cause analysis: the
cancellation feature was built to meet minimum requirements (release the slot) without
considering the notification ecosystem that was designed in parallel. Gap was identified
on Nov 1 at 2:47 PM during standup. Decision made to delay Sprint 2 completion by two
days to implement a proper solution. Emergency design meeting convened with James, Kai,
Sophia, and Amelia. No customer impact because system remains in staging; no production
trial has commenced. Team confidence remains high because the issue was caught before
external testing.

================================================================================

ENTRY 6: November 2, 2026

Repair implementation commenced for the notification gap. Architecture decided upon:
when a cancellation occurs, the system logs a CANCELLATION event in a new
CancellationEvents table with timestamp, location_id, and released_slot_id. A
background job (scheduled via node-cron, runs every 2 minutes) queries for new
cancellation events, then identifies all patrons with active appointments within 45
minutes before or after the released slot time at the same location. System sends each
identified patron an email with subject line "New availability at [Location Name]" and
offers a one-click reschedule link pre-populated with the newly freed slot. This preserves
the 30-minute cancellation window constraint (patrons get notified immediately, not after
a delay) and creates genuine value for other patrons without overwhelming them with emails
(only adjacent-time patrons get notified, not all patrons everywhere). Implementation
required: (1) new CancellationEvents table, (2) update cancellation endpoint to log event,
(3) new background job file with error handling and logging, (4) new email template for
availability alerts, (5) integration tests for the complete flow. All five components
completed and deployed to staging by end of day November 2. Database migration included
rollback script. New cron job tested by artificially triggering cancellation events and
verifying emails arrived within 120 seconds. Email delivery confirmed via staging mail
server logs. No syntax errors or runtime exceptions observed during 50-scenario test run.

================================================================================

ENTRY 7: November 3, 2026

Comprehensive regression testing resumed to verify the repair did not break existing
functionality. Test matrix: (1) normal booking flow unchanged - PASS, (2) cancellation
within 30-min window - PASS, (3) cancellation outside 30-min window (no change) - PASS,
(4) notification delivery for adjacent patrons - PASS, (5) notification does not send to
unaffected patrons - PASS (verified by checking email logs; only targeted patrons
received alerts), (6) rescheduling to newly freed slot - PASS, (7) race condition between
cancellation event log and cron job (cron fires before event logged) - edge case tested,
PASS (idempotency ensures duplicate events do not create duplicate emails), (8) cron job
failure recovery (job throws exception) - tested via forcibly breaking job logic, verified
that error logged and next cron cycle retried, PASS. Staging database now contains 12,000
synthetic appointment records (generated via data factory script by Sophia), 400 canned
cancellation scenarios, and 800 rescheduling transactions. Load test run: system processed
all 400 cancellation events with avg email delivery in 87ms, 95th percentile at 310ms. No
database deadlocks, no queue overflow, no lost events. Marcus conducted one final walkthrough
of the release slot logic and confirmed no orphaned appointment records remained after
cancellation. One cosmetic issue found in email template (extra newline in sender name);
corrected by Amelia. All systems ready for trial prep milestone. Current status: no known
defects. Code quality metrics: 93% unit test coverage on modified cancellation code, 87%
on email notification modules.

================================================================================

ENTRY 8: November 4, 2026

Soft launch readiness review conducted by Captain Davidson (project sponsor). Team
presented: feature completion status (100% of Sprint 2 scope + gap repair), test evidence
(regression results, load test summaries, database integrity checks), and trial plan.
Trial plan proposes: limited internal pilot with 25 fictional staff members from each of
three library branches (75 total), running for two weeks, with daily sync meetings to
track issues. Captain requested independent evidence of notification reliability. Concern
raised: team's email delivery tests were conducted against staging mail server, not
production infrastructure. In production trial, email delivery will route through actual
Sendgrid account (not yet configured). Team acknowledged the evidence gap: we can show
that notification logic triggers correctly in staging, but we have not validated end-to-end
email delivery through production systems. Recommendation made to configure Sendgrid staging
environment and re-run load test against it before trial greenlight. Captain asked: "What
happens if we postpone the trial two weeks?" Answer: Sendgrid validation will complete,
new feature enhancement for patron preferences (booking frequency limits) can be implemented,
and team will have built additional margin for unexpected issues. If trial proceeds on
schedule (Nov 15), team runs production Sendgrid config on November 14 one-off, with no
validation under load. Captain decision pending. Next sync scheduled November 5 (today).

================================================================================

ENTRY 9: November 5, 2026 (Morning Update)

Preliminary Sendgrid staging environment configuration completed. API keys obtained and
integrated into staging deployment. Initial connectivity test successful: 10 test emails
sent via Sendgrid staging, all delivered within 2 seconds, verified in Sendgrid dashboard.
Database schema updated to include notification send status tracking (queued, sent,
bounced, failed). New NotificationStatuses table created with fields for event_id,
recipient_email, send_timestamp, sendgrid_message_id, delivery_status. Deployment to
staging completed. Integration test framework expanded to query NotificationStatuses table
and verify correct status progression. Formal load test against Sendgrid staging planned
for this afternoon: will trigger 400 synthetic cancellation events, each generating
notification for 3-5 patrons, simulating 1200-2000 outbound emails within 10-minute window.
Expected batch delivery time under normal conditions: 30-45 seconds, well within
operational tolerance for library staff who monitor appointment changes. Test script
written by Kai, review by James pending. Current blockers: none. One clarification needed
from Captain Davidson: after load test completes successfully today, does this evidence
satisfy the production readiness gate for Nov 15 trial launch, or does Captain want
additional validation? Awaiting guidance.

================================================================================

ENTRY 10: November 5, 2026 (Afternoon Update)

Load test against Sendgrid staging completed at 3:47 PM. Test harness triggered 412
simulated cancellation events across three locations over 12-minute period. Total
notifications generated: 1,847 emails (average 4.48 recipients per cancellation). Sendgrid
received all 1,847 requests successfully. Delivery status tracking: 1,841 marked delivered
within 60 seconds, 6 marked delivered within 120 seconds (Sendgrid rate-limiting behavior
under load, expected and acceptable). Zero bounces, zero failures. Average email delivery
latency: 47 milliseconds from cancellation trigger to Sendgrid acceptance. Staging mail
inbox received all emails correctly; spot-check of 20 random emails verified correct
patron names, correct released slot times, correct reschedule links. Database integrity
check post-test: all 1,847 notification records present in NotificationStatuses table with
correct timestamps and delivery status. No duplicate sends detected. Cron job error logs
clean (no exceptions or warnings). Sophia conducted audit of database transaction logs and
confirmed no constraint violations or deadlocks during the 12-minute test window. Final
verdict: production Sendgrid infrastructure readiness confirmed. Evidence: staging load
test demonstrates correct behavior under 1,847-email volume. Evidence limitation: staging
infrastructure may differ from production capacity in ways not captured by test. However,
Sendgrid claims to handle millions of emails daily, so 1,847 is well within safety margin.
Recommendation to Captain: trial launch on November 15 is supported by current evidence.
If trial is postponed two weeks to November 29, team can: (1) deploy to true production
Sendgrid environment and run validation test there, (2) complete patron-preference
feature implementation, (3) harden error recovery in background cron jobs. Either path
is viable. Decision deferred to Captain Davidson pending final review. Team stands ready
for either outcome.

================================================================================

END OF REPORT

# PROJECT LANTERN 6 STATUS REPORT
## Community Library Appointment Pilot

---

## ENTRY 1: 2026-08-15
**Status: Kickoff**

Project Lantern 6 launches as a four-week pilot to test appointment-booking software across three branch libraries in the Westbrook system: Central, Harbor, and Riverside. The scope is narrow and concrete. Patrons will book thirty-minute library consultation slots—resume review, homework help, technology assistance—using a web form and SMS confirmation flow. We are integrating with the existing library patron database (LIS v4.2) and SMS gateway (Twilio). The hypothesis is that structured booking reduces staff friction, cuts no-shows below fifteen percent, and surfaces demand patterns that justify expansion to all eight branches.

Test environment: two staff machines at Central running build 0.8.1, sandbox credentials, test patron accounts. We seeded fifty fake bookings across the three branches using a CSV import script written in Python. The form validation passed all smoke tests. SMS sending works in sandbox mode. The booking confirmation email template renders correctly across Outlook and Gmail. Cancellation flow exists but was not thoroughly tested in kickoff week—noted for week two. No blockers reported.

---

## ENTRY 2: 2026-08-22
**Status: Early Integration Testing**

Week two focused on real patron workflow and staff dashboards. Central branch brought in five volunteer staff members (Susan, Marcus, Tanya, Jackson, and Leo) and they each booked and kept three test appointments. The form UX passed: no dropout. Confirmation SMS arrived within two minutes. Staff dashboard showed bookings, patron contact info, and time-block occupancy. The system correctly locked out new bookings when staff marked a slot "in progress."

We discovered one minor issue: the SMS template showed patron name but not appointment type, making it hard for patrons to remember whether they booked tech help or resume review. We pushed a one-line template fix (adding appointment type to the SMS body). The fix deployed to sandbox Friday afternoon and tested successfully Monday morning with new test bookings.

Cancellation flow was tested informally by Susan, who clicked "cancel appointment" from the patron portal. The booking disappeared from her view. However, we did not verify that the booking was removed from the staff dashboard, that the time slot became available again for rebooking, or that a cancellation confirmation SMS was sent to the patron. This gap was noted in the test log but not flagged as urgent—cancellations are expected to be rare in a pilot with committed volunteers. Retrospectively, this was a mistake.

---

## ENTRY 3: 2026-08-29
**Status: Pilot Launch**

August 29 marks the public opening of appointment booking at all three branches. Marketing materials (posters, email, SMS outreach to active patrons) went live Monday morning. Staff received a two-hour training session at each branch: how to mark appointments "complete," how to view no-show reports, how to handle patrons calling to cancel over the phone. By end of week, we had accumulated eighty-six bookings across the three locations. No-show rate was eight percent (seven patrons did not arrive; two called ahead to reschedule over voice). The form remained stable. SMS delivery rate was 100% for confirmation messages.

However, at 4 PM Thursday, Harbor branch manager Dale called the project lead (Rebecca) to report a problem. A patron, Ms. Chen, booked a resume-review appointment for 2 PM the same day. At 1:30 PM she called the library to cancel because her work schedule changed. The staff member answered the phone and told her the cancellation was confirmed. But the next day, Ms. Chen received an SMS reminder saying her appointment was still scheduled for tomorrow. She called back, confused. When Rebecca checked the portal, the appointment was indeed still marked "active" on the staff side, meaning the time slot was not available for anyone else to book. This was the first concrete evidence that the cancellation flow was broken.

---

## ENTRY 4: 2026-09-05
**Status: Cancellation Flow Gap Confirmed**

Investigation revealed the full scope of the cancellation bug. The patron-facing cancellation button correctly removed the booking from the patron's personal view (the "My Appointments" page). However, it did not write a cancellation state to the database—it only set a client-side session flag. As a result, the backend still considered the slot occupied, the staff dashboard still showed the appointment, and the automated reminder SMS still fired based on the original booking time.

We found four more instances of this issue in the logs between August 29 and September 4. In two cases, patrons called to complain about reminder SMS for appointments they thought they had cancelled. In one case, a patron attempted to re-book the same time slot and received an error message saying it was unavailable, when in reality the original booking had never been cancelled server-side.

Root cause: the cancellation endpoint was never wired to the database schema. The feature was documented in the UI mockup but skipped during backend implementation—a gap between the design spec and the code. The developer assigned to the cancellation feature (Mark) had moved to another project and the task fell through. It was never caught during the initial code review because the reviewer (Janet) verified that the cancellation button existed and the page did not crash, but did not test the backend state. No integration test existed for the cancel-and-rebooking workflow.

---

## ENTRY 5: 2026-09-12
**Status: Cancellation Repair**

We halted new public signups on September 5 and issued a temporary notice on the library website: "Cancellations by phone only; online cancellation is temporarily unavailable." This preserved data integrity while we developed a fix.

The repair involved three changes. First, we rewired the cancellation endpoint to write a "cancelled" state to the appointment table in the LIS database, including a timestamp and the user ID of whoever initiated the cancellation (either the patron or a staff member). Second, we modified the staff dashboard query to filter out cancelled appointments from the active list. Third, we added logic to the SMS reminder job: skip sending reminders for appointments marked cancelled.

We also added a new database view to surface cancellation metrics: date, branch, appointment type, and reason (when provided). This was a direct request from Rebecca and the branch managers, who wanted to understand why patrons cancel and whether patterns emerge around certain appointment types or time slots.

The fix was code-reviewed by Janet and Dmitri (a fresh pair of eyes, new to the project). They verified the SQL migration was syntactically correct, the endpoint logic matched the design, and no existing queries would break. We tested locally with one hundred mock cancellations across various appointment types and branches. All cancellations wrote correctly to the database. Rebooking the same slot after cancellation succeeded. Reminder SMS was correctly suppressed. We then deployed to staging and ran a full end-to-end test: Rebecca booked an appointment as a patron, a staff member cancelled it from the staff dashboard, a second staff member rebooked the slot thirty seconds later, and both patrons received correct SMS messages.

Testing completed September 11. Public signups resumed September 12 at 8 AM.

---

## ENTRY 6: 2026-09-19
**Status: Post-Repair Validation**

Week three of the pilot, after the cancellation repair. Total bookings now at 240. No-show rate held at nine percent. Cancellation rate is now measurable: we logged thirty-two cancellations across the three branches (13% of all bookings). The reasons, when patrons provided them, centered on schedule changes (eighteen), illness (seven), and rescheduling to a different time (four). Three cancellations had no reason recorded.

We observed that Central branch had a slightly higher cancellation rate (16%) compared to Harbor (11%) and Riverside (10%). Rebecca is investigating whether this reflects patron demographics, marketing message clarity, or scheduling patterns at that location. No conclusion yet, but this insight would have been impossible before we fixed the cancellation flow.

One limitation emerged during this review: the SMS reminder job does not capture whether reminders are actually delivered. We know when Twilio accepts our API call, but not whether the SMS arrives on the patron's phone or bounces. Mark (who has now re-joined the project) flagged this as a gap if we want to measure reminder effectiveness. For the current pilot, we are treating this as out of scope—the system behaves as designed—but Rebecca has noted it for the post-pilot retrospective.

Staff feedback continues to be positive. All three branch managers report that the appointment bookings are reducing ad-hoc scheduling conversations, and one manager noted that the system helps her see which appointment types are overbooked. No critical issues reported.

---

## ENTRY 7: 2026-09-26
**Status: Pilot Conclusion and Data Summary**

The four-week pilot ended September 26. Final bookings: 318 across the three branches. Attendance rate: 91% (29 no-shows). Cancellation rate: 12% (39 cancellations). The majority of no-shows occurred at Harbor branch (18 no-shows, 12% of Harbor's 150 bookings), suggesting a possible need for reminder SMS frequency adjustments at that location. Average patron satisfaction feedback (collected via a post-appointment SMS survey): 4.1 out of 5 stars, with 94 responses out of 318 invited.

The cancellation flow is now stable. In the final two weeks of the pilot, zero cancellation-related bugs were reported. The repair held. We did not observe any more ghost appointments or failed rebookings. Confidence in the cancellation state is high.

Evidence limitations: We did not measure whether the time between booking and appointment affects no-show rates (e.g., same-day bookings might have higher no-show rates than week-ahead). We did not track which staff members completed appointments, so we cannot determine if certain staff availability correlates with popularity. The SMS reminder frequency is fixed at 24 hours before; we do not have data on what frequency would optimize attendance. These gaps do not invalidate the pilot but constrain the conclusions we can draw.

---

## ENTRY 8: 2026-10-03
**Status: Expansion Proposal and Captain Decision Gate**

Proposal under review: expand Project Lantern 6 to four additional library branches (North, South, East, and Extension) in a controlled internal trial. The scope mirrors the original pilot—thirty-minute consultation slots, same SMS and email workflows, same LIS integration. The timeline is six weeks (October 10 to November 21), with the goal of validating that the system scales and operates reliably beyond the three original branches.

A formal sign-off is required from the Libraries Director (called "the Captain" in internal project language) before we can allocate budget, schedule staff training, and begin marketing to patrons at the four new branches. The trial will consume approximately 200 staff hours (training, coordination, troubleshooting across four locations) and will incur Twilio SMS charges estimated at $800 to $1200 depending on cancellation and reminder volumes.

Key question for the Captain's decision: the pilot succeeded, but the data set is small (318 bookings). Is it wise to proceed to an internal trial at four more branches, or should we wait until we have more pilot data to identify and address deeper issues (e.g., the Harbor branch no-show pattern, the SMS reminder effectiveness blind spot)? If the trial proceeds, we will observe those issues in a larger population, which could yield faster insights. If the trial is postponed, we can invest time in instrumentation—building better logging for SMS delivery, implementing A/B tests on reminder frequency—before expanding.

---

## ENTRY 9: 2026-10-10
**Status: Captain's Conditional Approval**

The Captain approved the internal trial with two conditions:

1. We must instrument SMS delivery tracking before going live. This means updating the Twilio integration to log delivery receipts (bounce, sent, failed) and building a dashboard to show delivery rates by branch and time of day. Cost: estimated 40 hours of engineering work.

2. We must implement a configurable reminder frequency setting so each branch can tune SMS reminders independently (e.g., Harbor can test 48-hour reminders instead of 24-hour). This allows us to test the no-show hypothesis without running parallel systems. Cost: estimated 20 hours.

Both features are in scope and do not conflict with the existing code. The team accepted the conditions. Engineering began on October 10. The feature branches are scheduled for code review and merge by October 22, giving us a one-week buffer before the new branches go live on October 31.

Current status: Dmitri is implementing the delivery logging (halfway complete). Mark is building the configurable reminder UI (backend schema changes in review). No blockers reported. We are on track.

---

## ENTRY 10: 2026-10-24
**Status: Trial Ready, Next Steps Defined**

Both instrumentation features merged and deployed to staging on October 22. Integration testing completed October 23. SMS delivery tracking works: we now see real-time delivery status for all outbound messages. The reminder frequency setting is live, and branch managers can adjust it from the staff dashboard. Central branch is testing 24-hour reminders; Harbor is testing 48-hour reminders; Riverside unchanged at 24-hour.

On October 31, we will open appointments at the four new branches (North, South, East, Extension). Staff training is scheduled for October 28-29. Marketing materials are ready. The LIS database has been populated with staff and room capacity data for the four new branches. SMS templates are configured.

The plan assumes the trial runs for six weeks as originally scheduled, concluding November 21. At that point, we will have observed over 600 additional bookings (projected), allowing us to assess whether the Harbor no-show pattern is a local issue or a systemic issue, and whether the 48-hour reminder frequency improves attendance. If the trial shows positive results, the proposal for full expansion to all eight branches will be strong.

If the trial is postponed beyond November 21, the project timeline slips by at least six weeks. Staff scheduling commitments would need to be renegotiated. Marketing delays would reduce early-trial booking volumes, weakening the data set. Momentum with branch managers would be at risk. A postponement is possible if critical issues emerge, but none are visible today.

All hands are ready. The Captain's decision gate is closed. The next checkpoint is November 21 with a trial outcome report.
